\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{গুরুত্ব} (gurutvô)}{গুরুত্ব (gurutvô)}]{\bn{গুরুত্ব} (gurutvô) — importance}

\label{lesson:BN-C336-gurutvo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an example, then the Bengali for a topic of talk.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{গুরুত্ব}}
\textbf{\bn{গুরুত্ব}} — \emph{gurutvô} — \textquotedblleft{}importance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এই} \bn{সিদ্ধান্তের} \bn{গুরুত্ব} \bn{অনেক।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ei siddhānter gurutvô ônek.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This decision matters a great deal.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{গুরুত্ব}} (\emph{gurutvô}) is Sanskrit \emph{gurutva}, weight (Monier-Williams), from \emph{guru} 'heavy'. Bengali uses the weight for importance, as English speaks of a weighty matter.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gurutvô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ei siddhānter gurutvô ônek.} — This decision matters a great deal.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an example, then the Bengali for a topic of talk, then say \emph{gurutvô} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বিশেষ} (bishesh)}{বিশেষ (bishesh)}]{\bn{বিশেষ} (bishesh) — special; particular}

\label{lesson:BN-C336-bishesh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a topic of talk, then the Bengali for importance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বিশেষ}}
\textbf{\bn{বিশেষ}} — \emph{bishesh} — \textquotedblleft{}special; particular\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আজ} \bn{একটা} \bn{বিশেষ} \bn{দিন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āj ekṭā bishesh din.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Today is a special day.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বিশেষ}} (\emph{bishesh}) is Sanskrit \emph{viśeṣa}, a distinguishing mark (Monier-Williams). Before a noun it means special or particular.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a topic of talk, then the Bengali for importance, then say \emph{bishesh} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{মূল} (mūl)}{মূল (mūl)}]{\bn{মূল} (mūl) — main; chief; the root (of something)}

\label{lesson:BN-C336-mul}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for importance, then the Bengali for special.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{মূল}}
\textbf{\bn{মূল}} — \emph{mūl} — \textquotedblleft{}main; chief; the root (of something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{তোমার} \bn{বক্তব্যের} \bn{মূল} \bn{কথাটা} \bn{কী}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tomār bôktôbyer mūl kôthāṭā kī?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
What is the main point of what you are saying?
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{মূল}} (\emph{mūl}) is Sanskrit \emph{mūla}, a root, and so the basis or origin of a thing (Monier-Williams). Before a noun it means the main one, the one the rest grows from: \bn{মূল} \bn{কথা}, the main point.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mūl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mūl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tomār bôktôbyer mūl kôthāṭā kī?} — What is the main point of what you are saying?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for importance, then the Bengali for special, then say \emph{mūl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ব্যাখ্যা} \bn{করা} (bækhyā kôrā)}{ব্যাখ্যা করা (bækhyā kôrā)}]{\bn{ব্যাখ্যা} \bn{করা} (bækhyā kôrā) — to interpret; to explain in detail}

\label{lesson:BN-C336-bekhya-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for special, then the Bengali for main.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ব্যাখ্যা} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{ব্যাখ্যা} \bn{করা}} — \emph{bækhyā kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to interpret; to explain in detail\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{তুমি} \bn{এই} \bn{কবিতাটা} \bn{কীভাবে} \bn{ব্যাখ্যা} \bn{করবে}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tumi ei kôbitāṭā kībhābe bækhyā kôrbe?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
How will you interpret this poem?
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{আইনটা} \bn{ব্যাখ্যা} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini āinṭā bækhyā kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ব্যাখ্যা} \bn{করা}} (\emph{bækhyā kôrā}) is Sanskrit \emph{vyākhyā}, explanation or commentary (Monier-Williams), with \bn{করা}. It goes further than \bn{বোঝানো}: it lays out what a text or a law means.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tumi ei kôbitāṭā kībhābe bækhyā kôrbe?} — How will you interpret this poem?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for special, then the Bengali for main, then say \emph{bækhyā kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সংক্ষেপে} (sôngkkhepe)}{সংক্ষেপে (sôngkkhepe)}]{\bn{সংক্ষেপে} (sôngkkhepe) — briefly; in short}

\label{lesson:BN-C336-songkkhepe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for main, then the Bengali for to interpret.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সংক্ষেপে}}
\textbf{\bn{সংক্ষেপে}} — \emph{sôngkkhepe} — \textquotedblleft{}briefly; in short\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সংক্ষেপে} \bn{বলো}, \bn{কী} \bn{হল}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sôngkkhepe bôlo, kī hôlô?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Tell me briefly, what happened?
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সংক্ষেপে}} (\emph{sôngkkhepe}) is Sanskrit \emph{saṃkṣepa}, a condensing or abridgment (Monier-Williams), with the Bengali ending -\bn{এ}: 'in brief'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}
